req.title: Reject non-GET on /get
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed for any non-GET request to /get.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /get must accept GET requests (HTTP 200) and reject all non-GET methods with HTTP 405. The route is defined with methods=("GET",), so Flask will automatically return 405 for POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD (non-standard), etc. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — valid GET returns 200 with correct payload keys; (2) negative EP — POST returns exactly 405; (3) negative EP — PUT returns exactly 405; (4) negative EP — DELETE returns exactly 405; (5) negative EP — PATCH returns exactly 405; (6) boundary DT — HEAD method (allowed by Flask implicitly for GET routes) returns 200 not 405; (7) boundary BVA — status code is exactly 405, not 404 or 400. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill constant-mutation and comparison-mutation operators.

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'args' in data
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert 'origin' in data
    assert r.content_type == 'application/json'

trace: R-HTTPBIN-003: decision table — all non-GET methods must return 405; catches any method-specific branch mutation
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_multiple_non_get_methods_all_return_405():
    methods = [
        client.post,
        client.put,
        client.patch,
        client.delete,
    ]
    for method_fn in methods:
        r = method_fn('/get')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f"Expected 405 but got {r.status_code}"
